grammar.q: Take a coat. I think it ___ be cold in the mountains.

grammar.q: Those bags look heavy. I ___ help you carry them.

grammar.q: How ___ luggage have you got?

grammar.q: How ___ suitcases are you taking?

grammar.q: There ___ a lot of luggage on the train.

reading.title: A trip to Scotland
reading.text:
Last summer, Amy and her family went on holiday to Scotland. It was a long journey, so they took the train from London. The train left at eight o'clock in the morning and arrived in Edinburgh after four and a half hours. Amy read a book and looked out of the window at the hills and sheep.

In Edinburgh they stayed in a small hotel near the castle. Every day they visited a different place. Amy's favourite was a museum about dinosaurs. On the last day she bought a postcard for her best friend, Zara. On it she wrote: 'Scotland is beautiful, but it rains a lot! Next year I will come back with you!'

qs.q: How did Amy's family travel to Scotland?
How long was the train journey?
Where was the hotel?
Amy's favourite place was a museum about dinosaurs.
Amy wrote that the weather in Scotland was always sunny.

reading.title: Camping on an island
reading.text:
Last August, Tom and his family went camping on a small island. They took a boat from the coast with their rucksacks and a big tent. The journey only took forty minutes, but Tom felt a bit sick on the boat.

On the island there were no cars and no shops. Every day they swam in the sea, walked along the beach and looked for shells. One evening, while they were cooking dinner on a little fire, they saw dolphins jumping in the water!

On the last day, Tom found a beautiful white shell. He didn't buy a souvenir, because the shell was the best souvenir of all.

qs.q: How did they get to the island?
Tom felt a bit sick on the boat.
There were lots of shops on the island.
What did they see while they were cooking dinner?
Why didn't Tom buy a souvenir?
opts: The shell was the best souvenir.

extra.q: We arrived ___ the airport at six o'clock.

extra.why: When a plane takes off, it leaves the ground and goes up into the sky.

grammar.q: The cheetah is the ___ animal on land.
grammar.why: Use 'the' + -est to compare one thing with all the others: the fastest.

grammar.q: Mount Everest is the ___ mountain in the world.

reading.title: Busy bees
reading.text:
Bees are small, but they are some of the most important insects in the world. A bee has got four wings and six legs. It flies from flower to flower and drinks a sweet juice called nectar. Back at its home, the hive, it turns the nectar into honey.

Bees also help plants. When a bee visits a flower, yellow powder from the flower sticks to its body. The bee carries it to the next flower, and this helps fruit like apples and strawberries grow.

You can help bees too. Plant some flowers in your garden or in a pot by the window. Bees love blue and purple flowers best!

qs.q: How many wings has a bee got?
What is a hive?
Bees help fruit like apples to grow.
Bees like red flowers best.
What does a bee make from nectar?

reading.title: From egg to butterfly
reading.text:
Did you know that every butterfly starts its life as a tiny egg? A mother butterfly lays her eggs on a leaf. After a few days, a small caterpillar comes out of each egg. It is very hungry, so it eats leaves all day and grows very quickly.

When the caterpillar is big enough, it makes a hard case around its body. Inside, something amazing happens. After about two weeks, the case opens and a butterfly comes out! At first its wings are wet, so it waits in the sun until they are dry. Then it flies away to find flowers.

qs.q: Where does a mother butterfly lay her eggs?
What does the caterpillar eat?
The caterpillar grows very slowly.
How long does the caterpillar stay inside the hard case?
A new butterfly's wings are wet at first.

extra.q: Bees fly ___ flower to flower.
extra.why: We say 'from one place to another': from flower to flower.

extra.q: We must ___ care of our planet.
extra.why: We say 'take care of' something. It means 'look after' it.

extra.q: Please don't ___ your plastic bottles. We can recycle them!

extra.q: Bees are very small, ___ they are very important.

grammar.q: Have you ever ___ a real astronaut?

reading.title: What do you want to be?
reading.text:
Our teacher asked us, 'What do you want to be when you grow up?' Everyone had a different answer.

Jack wants to be a pilot because he loves planes. He has already flown to six countries with his family. Mia wants to be a dentist like her mum. She says it is an important job, and you should look after your teeth every day! Sam wants to be an astronaut. He has read lots of books about space, and he wants to be the first person on Mars.

I want to be a journalist. I love asking people questions and writing stories. Last week I wrote a story about our school for the local newspaper!

qs.q: Why does Jack want to be a pilot?
opts: He wants to go to Mars.

qs.q: What job does Mia's mum do?
Sam has read lots of books about space.
The writer wants to be an astronaut.
What did the writer write about last week?

reading.title: Aunt Rosa's jobs
reading.text:
My aunt Rosa has had lots of different jobs. When she left school, she worked as a shop assistant in a clothes shop. Then she became a hairdresser, but she didn't enjoy it very much.

Now Rosa is a chef in a busy restaurant. She starts work at eleven o'clock in the morning and finishes late at night. It is hard work, and she doesn't earn a lot of money, but she loves it. Her favourite dish is fish with lemon and rice.

Last month, a famous actor came to the restaurant. He ate Rosa's fish and said, 'This is the best fish I have ever eaten!'

qs.q: What was Rosa's first job?
Rosa enjoyed being a hairdresser very much.
What time does Rosa start work?
Rosa loves her job as a chef.
Who came to the restaurant last month?

extra.q: Firefighters often work ___ night.
extra.why: We say 'at night', but 'in the morning' and 'in the afternoon'.

extra.why: We say 'ask a question', not 'make', 'do' or 'say' a question.

extra.q: Firefighters ___ a very important job.
extra.why: We say 'do a job', not 'make' a job.

extra.why: Use 'as' to say what someone's job is: he works as a waiter.

grammar.q: I ___ reading a book when the phone rang.
grammar.why: Use was or were + -ing for something that was going on in the past. With I, use 'was'.

grammar.q: The children ___ playing in the garden when it started to rain.
grammar.why: With we, you and they (the children), use 'were' + -ing.

reading.title: The dragon who loved cake
reading.text:
Long ago, a small green dragon called Pip lived in a cave near a big castle. Pip wasn't scary at all. He loved cake more than anything!

One night, at midnight, while the king and queen were sleeping, Pip flew to the castle kitchen. The cook was making a huge chocolate cake for the princess's birthday. Suddenly she saw Pip at the window. She was very surprised, but Pip smiled and said, 'Please may I have a small piece?'

The cook laughed and gave him some cake. The next day, the princess invited Pip to her party. From that day, the dragon and the princess were best friends.

qs.q: Where did Pip live?
What were the king and queen doing when Pip flew to the castle?
Who was making a cake?
The cook was angry with Pip.
The princess invited Pip to her party.

reading.title: The giant on the mountain
reading.text:
Long ago, a giant lived on a mountain near a small village. He was very, very tall, so the people in the village thought he was dangerous. Nobody ever visited him.

One day, a brave young prince called Leo decided to climb the mountain. When he arrived at the top, the giant was planting flowers in his garden. 'Hello!' said the giant with a big smile. 'Would you like to help me? Nobody ever comes to see me.'

Leo stayed all afternoon. They planted flowers, played games and laughed a lot. The next day, Leo brought all the children from the village, and they had a picnic in the giant's garden. From that day, the giant always had lots of friends.

qs.q: Why did nobody visit the giant?
What was the giant doing when Leo arrived?
The giant was angry when he saw Leo.
Leo stayed with the giant all afternoon.
Who did Leo bring the next day?

extra.q: Pip was hungry, ___ he flew to the kitchen.
extra.why: Use 'so' to say what happened because of something: he was hungry, so he flew to the kitchen.

extra.q: The story happened ___ the twelfth century.
extra.why: Use 'in' with centuries, years and months: in the twelfth century.

extra.q: The princess was happy ___ she found her lost ring.

extra.q: The pirates spent many years ___ the lost treasure.

grammar.q: If you play games all night, you ___ be tired tomorrow.

grammar.q: I have ___ downloaded the new game. Do you want to play?
grammar.why: 'Just' means a very short time ago. It goes between 'have' and the verb.

grammar.q: Have you finished your homework ___?
grammar.why: Use 'yet' at the end of present perfect questions and negatives.

grammar.q: This laptop is ___ heavy. I can't carry it.
grammar.why: 'Too' means more than is good: too heavy to carry.

grammar.q: Can you give me some ___ about the new phone?
grammar.why: 'Information' is uncountable: no -s and no 'an'.

grammar.q: If you don't charge your phone, it ___ work tomorrow.
grammar.why: First conditional: if + present simple, then won't (will not) + verb for the result.

grammar.q: I've ___ finished my homework, so I can play now.
grammar.why: 'Already' means before now, maybe sooner than you think. It goes between 'have' and the verb.

grammar.q: How ___ emails did you get today?
grammar.why: 'Emails' are countable (one email, two emails), so use 'how many'.

grammar.q: I ___ typing my story when the screen went black.
grammar.why: Use 'was' + -ing with I for something that was going on in the past.

sentences: Have you downloaded the new game yet?
My brother is too young to play this game.
Don't tell anyone your password.
I need a new battery for my camera.
Don't forget to save your work!
Can you send me an email?

reading.title: Ella's screen time
reading.text:
Ella is eleven and she loves gadgets. She has got a laptop, a tablet and some big blue headphones. Every evening she goes online to play games with her friends or watch videos.

Last month, Ella started to get headaches, and she often felt tired at school. Her mum said, 'I think you are spending too much time in front of screens. If you switch off your tablet an hour before bed, you will sleep better.'

Ella wasn't happy at first, but she tried it. Now she reads a book before bed instead. She has already finished three books this month, and her headaches have stopped. 'I still love my games,' she says, 'but books are fun too!'

qs.q: What does Ella do online every evening?
opts: She plays games and watches videos.

qs.q: What did Ella's mum tell her to do?
opts: switch off her tablet an hour before bed
play more games with her friends

qs.q: Ella was very happy with her mum's idea at first.
How many books has Ella finished this month?
Ella's headaches have stopped.

reading.title: Grandpa goes online
reading.text:
Last year my grandpa bought his first smartphone. At first he didn't like it at all. 'The buttons are too small,' he said, 'and I can't type fast enough!'

So every Sunday I helped him. First I showed him how to send a message. Then he learned how to search for information about his favourite football team. Now he sends me an email every morning, and he uses an app to talk to my cousin in Australia.

Last week Grandpa sent me a message: 'I've just downloaded a game. If you come on Saturday, I will beat you!' I think he loves his phone more than I love mine now!

qs.q: What did Grandpa think about his phone at first?
opts: He thought it was too big.

qs.q: When did the writer help Grandpa?
Grandpa uses an app to talk to the writer's cousin.
Grandpa sends the writer an email every evening.
What has Grandpa just downloaded?

extra.q: Can you ___ the music, please? It's too loud.
extra.why: 'Turn down' means make it quieter. 'Turn up' means make it louder.

extra.q: I found the information ___ the internet.
extra.why: We say 'on the internet' and 'on a website'.

extra.q: Type your name and password to ___ to the game.
extra.why: 'Log in' means type your name and password to start using a website or a game.

extra.q: Always use the internet ___ (safe).
extra.why: We need an adverb with -ly to say how you use it: safely.

units.title: Music and art

words.def: a show where people play music or sing for a lot of people
words.ex: We bought tickets for the ___ and listened to our favourite band.

words.def: a thing that you play to make music, like a piano or a drum
words.ex: The guitar is my favourite ___. I play it every day.

words.def: a big instrument with black and white keys that you press
words.ex: There's a big ___ at school, and our teacher plays it while we sing.

words.def: a small wooden instrument with strings that you hold under your chin
words.ex: She holds the ___ under her chin and plays it with a bow.

words.def: a metal instrument that you play by blowing into it
words.ex: He blew into the ___ and it made a very loud noise.

words.def: a person who sings, often as a job
words.ex: The ___ in the band has got a beautiful voice.

words.def: a short piece of music with words that you sing
words.ex: Let's sing a ___ for Grandpa's birthday!

words.def: a person who dances, often as a job
words.ex: The ___ jumped and turned on the stage in her ballet shoes.

words.def: a picture that someone makes with paint
words.ex: There is a famous ___ of a smiling woman in a museum in Paris. Leonardo da Vinci painted it.

words.def: a picture that you make with a pencil or a pen
words.ex: Look at my ___ of a horse. I did it with a pencil.

words.def: a building where people can look at paintings and other art
words.ex: My uncle's paintings are in a ___ in London, and people can buy them.

words.def: a model of a person or an animal made of stone or metal
words.ex: In the middle of the square there is a big ___ of a king on a horse.

words.def: red, blue, green and yellow are all examples of this
words.ex: Purple is my favourite ___.

words.def: to do something again and again to get better at it
words.ex: If you want to play the violin well, you have to ___ every day.

words.def: known by lots and lots of people
words.ex: Everyone knows that singer. She's very ___.

words.def: the high floor in a theatre or a hall where people sing, dance or act
words.ex: The actors walked onto the ___ and everyone clapped.

words.def: a person who plays music, often as a job
words.ex: My uncle is a ___. He plays the piano and the guitar in a band.

words.def: making a lot of noise
words.ex: The music at the concert was so ___ that I put my hands over my ears.

words.def: to hit your hands together again and again to show you like something
words.ex: At the end of the show, everyone stood up to ___.

words.def: something you get when you win a competition
words.ex: Leo's painting won first ___ in the school art competition.

grammar.q: I ___ practising the piano when you phoned.
grammar.why: With I, use 'was' + -ing: I was practising when you phoned.

grammar.q: Have you ever ___ a real orchestra?
grammar.why: Present perfect: have + past participle. 'Hear' is irregular: hear, heard.

grammar.q: I have ___ played the trumpet, but I'd like to try.
grammar.why: 'Never' means not at any time in your life: I have never played it.

grammar.q: The trumpet is the ___ instrument in our band.
grammar.why: Short adjectives add -est: loud, the loudest.

grammar.q: The song ___ won the competition was about the sea.
grammar.why: Use 'which' for things, like songs: the song which won.

grammar.q: If you practise every day, you ___ get better.
grammar.why: First conditional: if + present simple, then will + verb.

grammar.q: You ___ clap at the end of the song, not in the middle.
grammar.why: Use 'should' + verb (with no 'to') to say what is the right thing to do.

grammar.q: How ___ music do you listen to every day?
grammar.why: 'Music' is uncountable, so use 'how much'.

grammar.q: What ___ the children doing when the music stopped?
grammar.why: 'The children' means they, so use 'were' + -ing: What were they doing?

grammar.q: The concert finishes at ten, so I think we ___ get home before eleven.
grammar.why: Use 'won't' (will not) + verb to say what you think will not happen.

sentences: Have you ever heard a real orchestra?
Which instrument do you want to learn?
My sister is learning to play the violin.
The singer has got a beautiful voice.
Who painted this famous picture?
Is the music too loud for you?

reading.title: The school concert
reading.text:
Last Friday our school had a big concert in the hall. Parents, grandparents and teachers came to watch. First, the youngest children sang a funny song about a cat. Then my friend Max played the trumpet. He was very nervous, but he played really well.

I play the violin, and I practised every day for three months before the concert. When I walked onto the stage, my hands were shaking a little. But when I started to play, I felt happy. At the end, everyone stood up and clapped. Our music teacher said, 'That was the best concert we have ever had!'

qs.q: Where was the concert?
What did the youngest children do?
Max played badly because he was nervous.
How long did the writer practise before the concert?
At the end, everyone stood up and clapped.

reading.title: A day at the gallery
reading.text:
On Saturday, Lily and her mum went to an art gallery in the city. The gallery had paintings, drawings and statues from all over the world.

Lily's favourite painting was very big and full of colour. It showed a busy market with hundreds of people. 'How long did the artist take to paint this?' Lily asked. 'Two years,' said the guide.

In the last room, children could paint their own pictures. Lily painted a picture of her cat with bright orange and purple colours. The guide liked it so much that she put it on the wall for a week. Lily was very proud. 'I think I'll be a famous artist one day!' she said.

qs.q: Who did Lily go to the gallery with?
What did Lily's favourite painting show?
The artist took two years to paint Lily's favourite painting.
What did Lily paint?
The guide put Lily's picture on the wall for a month.

extra.q: Let's ___ a song together!
extra.why: We sing a song. We say words and we tell stories.

extra.q: Who is the girl ___ the painting?
extra.why: We say a person is 'in' a painting or 'in' a photo.

extra.q: If you don't win the prize this time, don't ___! Try again next year.
extra.why: 'Give up' means stop trying.

extra.q: She sings ___ (beautiful).
extra.why: Use an adverb with -ly to say how she sings: beautifully.
